messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Hindi, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Hindi line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
समय सुबह के प्रारम्भ में था, और सूर्य उन तारों के साथ ऊपर की ओर उठ रहा था जो उसके साथ थे जब दिव्य प्रेम

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table (Step 3)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------|-----------------------|--------| | Temp' | “time” that existed | **समय** | time | OK | | era | copular predicate of existence | **था** | was | OK | | dal | preposition introducing the locative phrase “principio del mattino” | **के** | of / from | OK | | principio | “beginning” of the morning | **प्रारम्भ** | beginning | OK | | del | preposition linking “principio” to “mattino” | **के** | of | OK | | mattino | the daily period that is beginning | **सुबह** | morning | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction joining clauses | **और** | and | OK | | ’l | definite article “the” (Italian) | — *(omitted)* | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | sol | the celestial body that is moving | **सूर्य** | Sun | OK | | montava | progressive upward motion of the Sun | **उठ रहा था** | was rising | OK | | ’n | part of the idiom “’n sù”, directional preposition | **ऊपर** | up | OK | | sù | adverb completing the direction “upward” | **की ओर** | toward | OK | | con (1) | preposition introducing accompanying entities | **के साथ** | with | OK | | quelle | demonstrative adjective specifying the stars | **उन** | those | OK | | stelle | luminous bodies accompanying the Sun | **तारों** | stars | OK | | ch’eran | relative pronoun + verb “that were” | **जो** | which/that | OK | | con (2) | preposition marking accompaniment of “lui” | **के साथ** | with | OK | | lui | pronoun referring to the Sun | **उसके** | his / its | OK | | quando | subordinating conjunction introducing a temporal clause | **जब** | when | OK | | l’amor | noun “Love” (Divine) | **प्रेम** | love | OK | | divino | adjective qualifying “Love” as sacred | **दिव्य** | divine | OK |
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: **’l** – the Italian definite article has no direct counterpart in Hindi and is naturally omitted. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** issues were detected; all other source tokens are represented with appropriate Hindi equivalents that preserve the intended truth‑conditions.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Hindi script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Hindi text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
